hero.lead: A nation of 43.8 million at the crossroads of Asia, where land, snowmelt, minerals and young people remain the assets of record, whatever the government.

capital.heading: Finance that reaches the people directly.

register.name: Response Plan for Afghan Returnees 2026
register.detail: Launched 19 May 2026 · April to December 2026 · Border response $100.7 million · Reintegration $428.5 million
register.note: An estimated 2.7 million returnees from Iran and Pakistan
register.text: The plan of the United Nations and NGO partners for Afghans returning from Iran and Pakistan: cash, health, nutrition, water and transport at the border, then education, health, water, livelihoods, housing and land rights where they settle. It reaches water, shelter, education, health and livelihood.

register.name: EU humanitarian aid for Afghanistan, 2026
register.detail: Initial allocation for 2026 · Through UN agencies, international organisations and NGOs
register.note: About €2.1 billion of EU humanitarian aid since 1994
register.text: The European Commission’s humanitarian funding for Afghanistan in 2026, delivered through its partners: emergency food, health care, nutrition, education in emergencies, water, sanitation and hygiene, protection, shelter and disaster preparedness. It reaches food, water, shelter, education and health.

register.name: Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: 1 January to 31 December 2026
register.note: 21.9 million people in need; 17.5 million targeted
register.text: The United Nations appeal for Afghanistan in 2026. Humanitarian funding still carries much of the basics: food, water, health care and shelter for those with the least.

register.name: Community Resilience and Livelihoods, 2026 financing
register.detail: Announced 13 February 2026 · $95 million approved by the World Bank Board · $48 million by the ARTF Steering Committee · UNOPS
register.note: Now a $562 million project, extended to all 34 provinces
register.text: A grant that expands community-led support for livelihoods, essential services and climate resilience: cash-for-work, social grants for households that cannot take part, home-based livelihoods for women, and the repair of water reservoirs, irrigation channels and village roads. It carries livelihood, water and food together.

register.name: ADB grant for health services and farm inputs
register.detail: Approved 9 October 2025 · Asian Development Fund
register.note: Health services in 17 provinces; farm inputs for 161,000 households
register.text: An Asian Development Fund grant that continues essential health services in 17 provinces and provides inputs for crop and livestock production to at least 161,000 households. It carries two of the seven standards: health and food.

register.name: ADB grant for food assistance and resilience
register.detail: Approved 9 October 2025 · Asian Development Fund
register.note: Hunger hotspots and communities hit by natural hazards
register.text: Food assistance for households in hunger hotspots, community action against weather and natural hazards, and alternative livelihoods for communities hit by natural hazards, including the earthquake of 31 August 2025. It reaches food and livelihood together.

register.name: ADB emergency grant after the Nangarhar earthquake
register.detail: Approved 17 September 2025 · Asia Pacific Disaster Response Fund
register.note: Food assistance for about 60,000 people
register.text: A fast-tracked grant for life-saving food assistance, in kind or in cash, for about 60,000 people after the earthquake that struck Nangarhar Province on 31 August 2025.

register.name: Health Emergency Response, Second Additional Financing
register.detail: Approved 15 March 2025 · UNICEF and WFP
register.note: Essential health services; care for mothers and newborns
register.text: A second additional financing for the project that keeps essential health and nutrition services running in Afghanistan, with a sharper focus on the quality of care for mothers and newborns. UNICEF delivers the health services and the World Food Programme the nutrition work. It carries health and food.

register.name: Education Emergency Response, Additional Financing
register.detail: Grant agreements signed December 2024 · IDA grant SDR 52.6 million · ARTF grant $25 million · UNICEF
register.note: Plus a $25 million ARTF grant; delivered by UNICEF
register.text: Improves children’s access to learning and the conditions in the schools it supports.

register.name: Community Resilience and Livelihoods, Additional Financing, 2024
register.detail: Approved 30 April 2024 · IDA grant $84 million · ARTF $70 million · UNOPS
register.note: Short-term employment and essential services
register.text: Expands the project to more areas: short-term employment, essential services such as roads, sanitation and water supply, more livelihood opportunities for women, climate resilience, and jobs and services for returning Afghan migrants.

register.name: EMERGe
register.detail: Announced 3 April 2024 · ARTF grant · Aga Khan Foundation and the Afghan Credit Guarantee Foundation
register.note: Finance for micro and small enterprises
register.text: Expands access to finance for micro and small enterprises, with a focus on women and women-led businesses.

register.name: ARTF, Approach 3.0
register.detail: Endorsed by the World Bank Board, 15 February 2024
register.note: Grants through UN agencies and public international organisations
register.text: The current framework: IDA grants for basic services and livelihoods, delivered through UN agencies and other public international organisations.

register.name: ARTF, Approach 2.0
register.detail: Approved 1 March 2022 · Afghanistan Resilience Trust Fund
register.note: Delivered outside the authorities
register.text: More than $1.3 billion from the ARTF for health, education, food security, water and livelihoods, delivered through UN agencies and other partners rather than through government.

register.name: ADB grants through the United Nations
register.detail: Approved 25 January 2022 · Asian Development Fund
register.note: $200m UNICEF, $135m WFP, $65m FAO, $5m UNDP
register.text: Emergency food for more than 800,000 people, farm inputs for about 390,000 households, basic health care for about 5.3 million people, and community classes for about 264,000 children, with support for female secondary teachers and adolescent girls.

register.name: Afghanistan Humanitarian Trust Fund
register.detail: Established by the OIC, December 2021 · Managed by the Islamic Development Bank
register.note: Pledges of almost US$35 million by March 2024; 16 projects under way
register.text: Grants for agriculture, education, food security, health, irrigation, hygiene and livelihoods, delivered through implementing partners. Donors include the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre, the Saudi Fund for Development and the Kuwait Society for Relief.

register.name: ARTF, Approach 1.0
register.detail: Decided 10 December 2021 · ARTF funds · $100 million UNICEF, $180 million WFP
register.note: Transferred to UNICEF and the World Food Programme
register.text: The first step to repurpose funds in the ARTF portfolio: $100 million to UNICEF for essential health services and $180 million to the World Food Programme for food security and nutrition operations.

register.name: Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Institutional Support
register.detail: Approved 11 December 2020 · IDA $50 million · ARTF $150 million
register.note: Urban water
register.text: Improves access to and the quality of water supply in selected cities, and strengthens the capacity of the urban water utility, AUWSSC, which carries out the project.

register.name: CASA-1000 Electricity Transmission and Trade
register.detail: Approved 27 March 2014 · Regional · Work resumed in Afghanistan, December 2024 · Full implementation expected by end 2027
register.note: The whole regional project: Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan
register.text: A regional line to carry 1,300 megawatts of surplus summer hydropower from the Kyrgyz Republic and Tajikistan across Afghanistan to Pakistan. Work resumed in Afghanistan in December 2024, with payments to contractors made directly into offshore accounts; the World Bank expects the project to be fully implemented by the end of 2027.

register.name: CASA-1000 Community Support Program
register.detail: Approved 24 March 2014 · Trust fund TF-17012 · Revised closing date 30 June 2022
register.note: Electricity and community infrastructure along the line
register.text: A programme to provide access to electricity or other social and economic infrastructure services to communities along the CASA-1000 line in Afghanistan.

register.name: TAPI gas pipeline, Herat section
register.detail: Serhetabat to Herat, 153 km · Construction began 11 September 2024
register.note: The key Afghan section of the Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India pipeline
register.text: The key Afghan section of the Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India gas pipeline, under construction from Serhetabat to Herat since 11 September 2024. It matters for energy.

register.name: Trans-Afghan railway
register.detail: Signing of a framework agreement on a joint feasibility study set for Kabul, 17 July 2025
register.note: Uzbekistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan
register.text: A planned rail link to connect Uzbekistan with Pakistan via Afghanistan and give Central Asian States access to Pakistani seaports. Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that its Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister would visit Kabul on 17 July 2025 to sign the three countries’ Framework Agreement on Joint Feasibility Study.

register.name: Japan grant for alternative livelihoods and drug treatment
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 3 September 2026 · JICA and UNODC · 24 months
register.note: Badakhshan, Badghis, Helmand, Kandahar and Takhar; maximum amount
register.text: A Japanese grant, executed by UNODC, that promotes alternative livelihoods for poppy and former poppy farmers and supports drug use prevention, treatment and recovery services in five provinces. It reaches livelihood and health.

register.name: BRIDGE, resilience and reintegration
register.detail: 31 August 2026 · €10 million EU allocation to a €13.5 million initiative · 36 months · Aga Khan Foundation
register.note: Ten provinces; €3.5 million co-funded by the Aga Khan Foundation
register.text: An EU-funded initiative to strengthen the resilience and reintegration of returnees and internally displaced persons in ten provinces, through climate-smart and regenerative agriculture, jobs and community resilience. It reaches food and livelihood.

register.name: EU support for returnees, through IOM
register.detail: 21 June 2026 · New allocation · International Organization for Migration
register.note: High-return areas
register.text: A European Union allocation that lets IOM scale up help for displaced people and returnees in high-return areas: protection services, health, psychosocial support, livelihoods and recovery programmes, vocational training and support for small and medium enterprises. It reaches health and livelihood.

register.name: Japan grant for climate change adaptation in Kabul Province
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 8 February 2026 · JICA and UNOPS
register.note: Climate adaptation facilities and community disaster preparedness
register.text: A Japanese grant, executed by UNOPS, to build climate change adaptation facilities in Kabul Province and to help communities handle disaster risks linked to climate change. It matters for water, shelter and livelihood.

register.name: German support through the World Food Programme, UN agencies and NGOs
register.detail: 14 August 2025 · Federal Foreign Office and Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
register.note: Food and basic health care for returnees and border regions
register.text: Additional German funding, on top of existing support through the United Nations, for food and life-saving basic health care, focused on returning Afghans and people in border regions, especially women and children. It carries food and health.
by: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Most of the land is farmed or grazed, while 27.8% of people are undernourished.
items.alt: Terraced fields in an Afghan valley

items.name: The Snowmelt
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person, 2022
items.text: The mountains feed the rivers, and the rivers feed the fields.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Mineralised, delineated by the USGS, 2007
items.text: Copper and iron among known deposits; quantitative estimates exist for copper and rare earths.
items.alt: Mineral-bearing rock in the Afghan mountains

items.name: The Corridor
items.label: CASA-1000, the whole regional project
items.text: A line to carry Central Asian power across Afghanistan to Pakistan. The World Bank says work in Afghanistan resumed in December 2024.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Young, and three in four live outside cities.
items.alt: A street market in an Afghan city

items.name: Local seed dealers
items.text: Farmers redeem subsidised inputs by e-voucher through established networks of private seed enterprises and input dealers; certified seed with adequate fertiliser and good agronomic practices lifts wheat yields by 32.8 percent.

items.name: Karez revival
items.text: Check dams recharge the ground, and dried-up karez channels flow again in the south.

items.name: Turquoise Mountain
items.text: 150 historic or community buildings restored or rebuilt in old Kabul.

items.name: Pamir Energy
items.text: Surplus hydropower exported across the river, reaching about 40,000 people in Afghanistan.

items.name: Begum TV
items.text: Secondary school lessons by satellite, 21 hours a day, for girls learning at home.

items.name: FMIC, Kabul
items.text: A 176-bed hospital renowned for its cardiac surgery programme; it has served over two million patients from all 34 provinces.

items.name: Rumi Spice
items.text: Afghan saffron processed by 1,900 women, paid 1.5 times a living wage.

coverage.gap_text: Ten-year-olds in Afghanistan who cannot read a simple text. Education is the standard furthest from reach.

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: No national measure of housing quality

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: About 142 kWh a person a year, against 1,000

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: Girls after grade six; women at university. Over 90% of ten-year-olds cannot read.

guarantees.name: Health
guarantees.note: Women barred from medical training since December 2024

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above the national poverty line, April–June 2023
